g.text: diamond (C): a = 3.54 Å (COD 1541404; 24 cubic entries, spread 0.032 Å)
Si: a = 5.381 Å (COD 1526655; 15 cubic entries, spread 0.071 Å)
Ge: a = 5.6455 Å (COD 1563565; 8 cubic entries, spread 0.012 Å)
GaAs: a = 5.6537 Å (COD 9008845; 1 cubic entries, spread 0.000 Å)
AlAs: a = 5.6608 Å (COD 1540257; 2 cubic entries, spread 0.041 Å)
InP: a = 5.861 Å (COD 1010146; 4 cubic entries, spread 0.030 Å)

svg.text: Each line is a Bragg reflection; × marks where a (200)-type reflection is extinct. Notice (200) at about 32°: absent in Si, Ge and diamond (one kind of atom, the two halves of the
basis cancel), barely there in GaAs (Ga and As differ by 2 electrons, so f_A − f_B is small: about 0.1% of the strongest peak), strong in AlAs (13 against 33) and InP (49 against 15).
That is how XRD tells zincblende from diamond, and an ordered compound from a mix. Caveats: scattering factors are taken as Z (no fall-off with angle, no thermal motion), so
high-angle peaks are too strong; real Si shows a weak (222) from its bond charge.
